apathy

AP-uh-thee -- built from a Greek prefix meaning 'without' plus a root meaning 'feeling.' · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Apathy is a lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern.

Voter apathy was so widespread that barely a third of registered citizens bothered to cast a ballot.

Example

Such is the town's apathy that every seat in the auditorium sits empty for the town hall meeting, even though the decision being made will affect every resident's taxes for the next decade.

That widespread lack of interest or concern is exactly what apathy describes. Unlike 'anger,' which is an intense reaction, apathy is marked by the complete absence of strong feeling.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

indifference: Indifference is having no preference or feeling about one particular matter -- you know the question is there and it simply does not move you either way. Apathy is wider and heavier: a lasting lack of interest, enthusiasm, or energy for things in general, not just no opinion on a single question.

detachment: Detachment is deliberately keeping your own feelings out of a situation -- a chosen distance, the way a surgeon or a referee stays uninvolved on purpose. Apathy is not chosen at all: it is the flat absence of interest or concern, a state that settles over a person rather than a stance anyone decides to take.

boredom: Boredom is restless dissatisfaction: you want something interesting to happen and nothing does, so the hours drag. Apathy has no wanting left in it -- a person sunk in apathy is not hungry for stimulation; they have stopped caring whether anything interesting happens at all.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

enthusiasm: intense and eager enjoyment or interest

passion: a strong and barely controllable emotion or interest

Where it sits · how wide and lasting the not-caring is

unconcern → apathy → numbness

unconcern vs. apathy: Unconcern is milder than apathy -- unconcern can describe a passing lack of worry about one small thing, while apathy suggests a broader, more persistent lack of interest or concern.

numbness vs. apathy: Numbness goes further than apathy -- apathy is a lack of interest and concern, but numbness is the inability to feel anything at all, when even news that should hurt or delight produces no flicker of feeling.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — a-: without, not (Greek)

root — -path-: feeling, suffering (Greek (pathos))

suffix — -y: noun-forming ending (state, condition) (Greek (-eia))

Put it together: Greek a- ('without') plus pathos ('feeling, suffering') plus the noun ending -y names the state of being untouched by feeling -- the same pathos root behind sympathy and empathy.

Use the root in a new word: empathy: Her empathy was the first thing every one of her teachers mentioned at conferences.
